_about: The war plan (after release 1; off by default, and off the game is release 1's move for move). A computer staff that thinks a season ahead. Month by month a staff weighs each front and attacks where the whole front's strength ratio is good enough (open.json). That leaves three gaps a thoughtful commander would not: a front at even strength sleeps for years because nobody gathers the army at one place; an enemy foothold on the coast is watched and never thrown back; and reserves answer only the enemy standing next door. With 'on' true, at the dial's 'stops' (the two where anything goes: at stop 3, in 24 wars with every staff planning, Germany fell a middle of four months sooner, which par at that stop does not allow until the design director rules on it), the staffs named in 'staffs' (empty: every computer-run nation with a staff character) plan campaigns. 'campaign': when the staff has attacked 'few' times or fewer in 'quiet' months on a front (a front gone quiet), a front whose ratio is at least 'ratio'[0] (under it the staff is on the strategic defensive) and under 'ratio'[1] (over it the ordinary offensive does the work), a staff that leads there (it has 'least' corps of its own fit to mass on the front, and they are the share 'own' or more of all its side has on it: a small ally on a greater army's front makes no plan of its own) picks the enemy province where the force it could gather (the best corps the roads into it can carry, tanks and guns first, from 'reach' marches around) would go in at 'strike' odds or better by the staff's own sums, weighing the road beyond it ('road' for the first province of the easiest road to his capital, 'beside' for its neighbours, less the going and 'works' for fortifications). It spends 'prep' months ([fewest, most]) massing: 'tanks' fast corps and infantry up to 'doors' at each of up to 'most' provinces next to the target, the rest of the line keeping what it needs. When the massed force has 'go' odds at the target by the battle's own reckoning the blow falls and is pressed for 'push' months whatever the front's ratio, as a general offensive along the road that starts where the army stands; if 'prep'[1] months pass without those odds the plan is dropped. After a campaign the front rests 'rest' months. 'foothold': an enemy piece of ground of 'size' provinces or fewer on this staff's own side's ground, with the sea behind it, is thrown back before it grows: where the staff's own sums give the force it can bring 'go' odds, and no other front with a real army on it stands under the ratio 'safe', it masses against it at once, whatever else it is doing ('tanks' fast corps and infantry up to 'doors' at each of up to 'most' provinces beside it), strikes at 'go' odds and presses for 'push' months; it keeps at it while the foothold has 'grown' provinces or fewer, after which it is a front like any other. 'recall': an army that has won its theatre goes back into the war. An army standing on friendly ground across the water, in one piece away from home, with no enemy on that ground or next to it and no battle on it or beside it for 'quiet' months, keeps a guard (one corps for each harbour of that ground an enemy's troopships can still reach, no fewer than 'least' and no more than 'most', the weakest of them; the corps an order holds in place and the landing force at the quay of the army abroad stay besides) and sends the rest, the strongest first, with the shipping left after the month's landings: into a harbour of a front its side holds across the water (its own landing first), where the test of strength lets a corps in; or home, to the landing quay; over no crossing riskier than 'risk', and from the harbours of Egypt round the Cape where the Mediterranean is too dangerous, the way they came (middle-east.json). Those not in a harbour march to the nearest one with a way out. Not for a staff whose army goes by the ocean runs. 'landing': with 'second' true, a staff whose men ashore are still too few but whose every harbour there is full, so that no ship can bring another corps, looks for a second shore as if it had none, where before it waited.
